### Packages needed
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
```

## Load Dataset
```{r}
df <- read_csv("df_sample.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

df$Year <- format(df$Date, format="%Y")

df<-df[!(df$PackageFocus %in% c("History","Standard Service","Shop") | df$Year=="2023"),]

```

## Distinct first-time and returning customers
This is done through the category variable which takes the value "first-time" if the customer is new and "returning" if the customer is old.
```{r}
df <- df %>% 
  group_by(TransactionId, CustomerId) %>% 
  mutate(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(category=ifelse(count==1, "first-time", "returning"))
```

## The 4 most sold PackageFocus
```{r}
order_count <- as.data.frame(table(df$PackageFocus))
colnames(order_count) <- c("PackageFocus", "count")
order_count <- order_count[order(-order_count$count),][1:4,]

ggplot(order_count, aes(y=reorder(PackageFocus, count), x=count))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity",fill="lightblue")+ geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = 0.4) + 
  labs(y = "PackageFocus", x = "Count")
```


The 4 most sold PackageFocus are : 
- Oil Change with 20508 sales
- Tire Package with 18622 sales
- State Inspection with 10073 sales
- Alignment with 5817 sales

## The 4 most store based on sales
```{r}
sales_count <- as.data.frame(table(df$StoreName))
colnames(sales_count) <- c("StoreName", "Sales")
sales_count <- sales_count[order(-sales_count$Sales),][1:4,]

ggplot(sales_count, aes(y=reorder(StoreName, Sales), x=Sales))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity",fill="lightblue")+ geom_text(aes(label = Sales), hjust = 0.4) + 
  labs(y = "StoreName", x = "Sales")
```

The 4 most store based on sales are :
- Windham with 2362 sales
- Saco with 2330 sales
- Yarmouth with 2192 sales
- Stratham with 2048 sales

# Most sales by year for fist-time and returning customer
```{r}

sales_df<-df[(df$PackageFocus %in% as.factor(order_count$PackageFocus) & (df$StoreName %in% as.factor(sales_count$StoreName))),]

ggplot(sales_df, aes(x=Year, fill=StoreName)) +
    geom_bar(position = "stack")+
    facet_wrap(~PackageFocus+category, ncol = 2,scales = "free_y")+
#   facet_grid(PackageFocus~category,scales = "free_y")+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines"),
        legend.key.size = unit(1.5, 'cm'))
```

We can directly notice an upward trend in sales per year for the best selling products with a strong increase in 2021.
Most of the orders on the best selling products come from new customers and they tend to come back less to buy the same product again.

# Growth (CAGR?) in sales of top packages

## First-time customers

```{r}
df_fc <- filter(df,category=="first-time")


df_fc$Year %>%
  aggregate(by=list(df_fc$Year, df_fc$PackageFocus, df_fc$StoreName), FUN = length) %>%
  filter(Group.2 %in% as.factor(order_count$PackageFocus) & Group.3 %in% as.factor(sales_count$StoreName)) %>%
  mutate(lagD = lag(x), #get lad Data
         t = 1, #calculate time
         CAGR = (x / lagD)^(1/t) - 1) %>%
  na.omit(.)%>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=Group.1, y=CAGR, fill=Group.3)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity",position="stack")+ 
    xlab("Year")+
    facet_wrap(~Group.2, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines"),
        legend.key.size = unit(1.5, 'cm'))
```


## Return customers

```{r}
df_fc <- filter(df,category=="returning")


df_fc$Year %>%
  aggregate(by=list(df_fc$Year, df_fc$PackageFocus, df_fc$StoreName), FUN = length) %>%
  filter(Group.2 %in% as.factor(order_count$PackageFocus) & Group.3 %in% as.factor(sales_count$StoreName)) %>%
  mutate(lagD = lag(x), #get lad Data
         t = 1, #calculate time
         CAGR = (x / lagD)^(1/t) - 1) %>%
  na.omit(.)%>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=Group.1, y=CAGR, fill=Group.3)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity",position = "stack")+
    xlab("Year")+
    facet_wrap(~Group.2, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines"),
        legend.key.size = unit(1.5, 'cm'))
```

From the last two graphs we can conclude: Whatever the sales store, there is a strong growth in sales of the selected products in 2021 and a slight increase in 2022.
